prompt.context: Your client is a leading manufacturer of nutrition bars (e.g. Kashi Go Lean bars, Powerbars) in the USA. The USA market is currently saturated so your client is looking to expand into other countries. You have one week to come up with the short list of countries to focus on.
prompt.question: How would you start? (Brainstorm a list of criteria to narrow the focus of countries — no time to structure a formal framework is allowed.)

clarifying_info.q: How is the client planning to enter the new market?
clarifying_info.a: The client is looking to start by importing the bars to the new country. Once the market is fully tested, a manufacturing facility will be created.

exhibits.title: Potential New Markets
exhibits.shows: A table comparing four candidate markets across two metrics: GDP (US$ Trillion) and Population (Billion). A note states that the cost per bar is about US$1 in every market.

data.note: Cost per bar is about US$1 in every market

exhibits.title: Potential New Markets: Demographics
exhibits.shows: A demographic breakdown table for the same four markets covering age distribution, median age, male-to-female ratio, urban population percentage, and average years of schooling.

framework: Market attractiveness: GDP size, GDP growth rate, overall geo-political situation
Consumer demand fit: GDP/capita, urban/suburban population, health-consciousness, proportion of working women
Regulatory environment: FDA-equivalent strictness, product classification (food vs. drug)
Cost to enter: import tariffs, transport and distribution costs, future manufacturing feasibility
Competitive landscape: existing competitors, market structure, potential competitor response

questions.prompt: Q1: Brainstorm criteria to narrow the list of countries to research within one week.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify criteria across market size (GDP, GDP growth), consumer profile (GDP/capita, urban population, health-consciousness, working women), regulatory hurdles (FDA equivalent, drug vs. food classification), cost (tariffs, transport, future manufacturing), and competitive dynamics. Answer should be spoken and written simultaneously — no formal framework structure is expected.

questions.prompt: Q2: Using Exhibit 1, rank your market preferences and explain. (Give Exhibit 1)
questions.guidance: Candidate must calculate GDP/capita to assess willingness to pay relative to a ~$1 bar. UK (GDP/capita ~$36,290) is the only market where the average consumer can clearly afford the product regularly. China's top 5% may be able to afford it and its high growth rate makes early-mover investment attractive. Brazil is mid-tier. India has the lowest GDP/capita. Candidate should also discuss ease of entry (UK most similar to US, lower corruption/tariff risk).

questions.prompt: Q3: Using Exhibit 2, re-rank your market preferences with demographic data and explain. (Give Exhibit 2)
questions.guidance: Candidate should form a hypothesis about the target consumer (teenagers to adults, urban, educated, corporate workers or athletes who treat bars as meal replacements or nutrition supplements). Women if Luna-style bars, men if protein-focused. Urban population and education level are key. Brazil (87% urban, 14 avg. years of school, growing/younger population) and UK (80% urban, 16 avg. years of school) rank best on demographics. UK is a mature market; Brazil is a high-growth emerging market. Any reasonable hypothesis with consistent justification is acceptable.

brainstorming.prompt: Brainstorm a list of criteria to narrow the focus of countries for market entry research.

categories.name: Market Size & Growth
ideas: GDP to estimate potential market size
GDP growth rate to estimate future market growth

categories.name: Consumer Demographics
ideas: Large urban/suburban population with corporate jobs or fitness lifestyle
Large working-women population (relevant for products like Luna bars)

categories.name: Regulatory Environment
ideas: Strictness of local FDA equivalent — additional testing required?
Product classification: food vs. drug (high-nutrition bars may be pharmacy-only in some countries)

categories.name: Cost to Enter
ideas: Import phase: transport, tariffs, distribution costs
Future manufacturing phase: government stability, pro-business tax incentives, labor and site costs

categories.name: Competition
ideas: Existing local competitors and market structure

recommendation: Enter UK first due to high GDP/capita (~$36,290), high urban population (80%), cultural and market similarity to the US, and low regulatory friction
Explore secondary entry into Brazil due to high urban population (87%), high average education (14 years), reasonable GDP/capita (~$10,526), and younger/growing consumer base
risks: Sacrificing early toehold in high-growth emerging markets (China, India)
Aggressive competitor response in UK, which is a mature market
next_steps: Conduct detailed UK market research: customer preferences, competitive landscape, and likely competitor response

Investigate the Chinese market further — identify the segment that can afford the product (~top 5%) and prepare for early entry to build brand and capture first-mover advantage as Chinese incomes grow
Evaluate market entry modes: joint venture, exports, or building a new local factory
